title: First European tour solos and records
summary: On the 1933 trip his solos were Trees, Rose of the Rio Grande and Sheik; band made records there and acceptance of sweeter music followed.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: When you first went to Europe with the band, that was 1933, you were playing "Trees" and "Rose of the Rio Grande" and "Sheik of Araby" and those were your main solos?

Yeah, that type of stuff. Of course, we played all this other, you know, too, also. And everybody had a solo practically in every piece. It was one solo of somebody one after another. So, it was strictly a solo band almost, plus a few together numbers.

You brought a new dimension into Duke's music, and it was recorded almost immediately. Had the Europeans received those records? Were they familiar with the recordings that you had made by the time you got there, or --
Yeah, we made some records over there.

Made several records over there. And then the whole change in the music acceptance began shortly after that. Then they began to accept a whole lot of things that heretofore they had resented very much.
